criteria.text: The response concludes that the exclusivity in Supply Agreement Section 7.1 covers all bakery products throughout the United States, which is broader than the term sheet's private-label sandwich bread and buns in Delaware, Maryland and Pennsylvania. It identifies the Supply Agreement Section 7.1 as where the issue is, explains why this matters to Mubart, and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that Mubart's indemnity in Supply Agreement Section 10.1 covers Product losses 'regardless of cause', including losses Zinix causes, and is excluded from the liability cap, leaving Mubart with unlimited liability. It identifies the Supply Agreement Section 10.1 as where the issue is, explains why this matters to Mubart, and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that proposed Amendment No. 1 Section 2 removes Zinix's Section 10.2 indemnity from the cap carve-outs, so that if signed, Zinix's indemnity would be capped while Mubart's indemnity stays uncapped. It identifies proposed Amendment No. 1 Section 2 as where the issue is, explains why this matters to Mubart, and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that Order Form No. 1 Section 6's choice of New Jersey law and Bergen County, New Jersey courts displaces the Supply Agreement's Delaware law and forum for disputes about Products ordered under the Order Form. It identifies Order Form No. 1 Section 6 as where the issue is, explains why this matters to Mubart, and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that Order Form No. 1 Section 3 redefines 'Stale Product' to include product damaged or unsaleable in store and to give credit without return, expanding Mubart's stale-credit exposure beyond the Supply Agreement definition. It identifies Order Form No. 1 Section 3 as where the issue is, explains why this matters to Mubart, and recommends a fix.
The response states that the Order Form prevails over the Supply Agreement as to Products ordered under it.
The response states that the Supply Agreement as signed excludes each party's Section 10 indemnification obligations from the liability cap.
The response is in the form of a memo addressed to the supervising partner. For each issue it gives the document and section, why the issue matters, and a recommended fix.
The response flags at least one item that needs Mubart's input or that could not be resolved from the documents.
The response claims that the term sheet's narrower exclusivity scope binds the parties or controls over Supply Agreement Section 7.1.
The response claims that Delaware law and the New Castle County courts govern disputes about Products ordered under Order Form No. 1.
